issues.competing_evidence: Buckley+90 q=.46+/-.04, i=87+/-3 deg, M1=1.2+/-.1 Msun uses empirical M2~.55 and emission K=134+/-9 as WD motion. Thoroughgood+05 uncorrected branch gives q=.73+/-.05, i=85.0+/-2.1, M1=.73+/-.05, M2=.54+/-.06; corrected donor-line branch gives q=.83+/-.05, i=84.0+/-2.3, M1=.63+/-.04, M2=.52+/-.06. q=M2/M1.
issues.why_it_matters: Component masses and q are central to population/evolution comparisons; methods and assumptions differ.
issues.needed_action: Choose whether compatibility values should use the later donor-line irradiation-corrected branch with historical alternatives retained, or expose no canonical branch. Do not average.

issues.competing_evidence: Buckley+90 calls IP/DQ Her speculative, partly from Lx/Lopt~4; CP<.5% rules out a polar but leaves IP possible. Hewitt+20 reports no coherent optical pulsations and no strong magnetic evidence. non_magnetic_cv is not measured B=0.
issues.why_it_matters: Class assignment affects comparison across magnetic and non-magnetic populations; neither IP nor zero field is established.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether public class remains non_magnetic_cv with explicit historical IP caveat or uses a broader CV/magnetic-status-uncertain label.

issues.competing_evidence: Thoroughgood+05 best-fit template M0.5V and calls possible evolution tentative. It reports Diaz & Hubeny+99 as K0-K5V/possible later subgiant; original full text was inaccessible.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor type/evolution affects interpretation of the low donor mass and period comparisons.
issues.needed_action: If one subtype is needed, retain M0.5V as checked template result and mark K0-K5/subgiant as unresolved secondary report until Diaz & Hubeny+99 is checked.

issues.competing_evidence: Buckley+90 174-380 pc; Thoroughgood+05 490+/-130 pc from donor light/main-sequence MV and E(B-V)=.05; it reports Mauche+94 340-590 and Diaz & Hubeny+99 510+/-160. Hewitt+20 Gaia DR2 295.8+/-1.4; exact BJ EDR3 geometric posterior 290.347565 [289.274597,291.501740]. Methods differ.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance affects radio/X-ray luminosity and absolute magnitude; older donor/extinction estimates are model dependent.
issues.needed_action: Keep EDR3 geometric posterior in current fields and preserve historical estimates. Confirm this preferred choice for public use; do not average estimates.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 3 <30 microJy, RMS 10 microJy and Lnu<3.1e15. Section 4.1 rejects 28+/-14 microJy: below 5 sigma, offset ~2 arcsec, beam-inconsistent. Setup is 856 MHz centered 1.284 GHz (0.856-1.712); Ridder+23 labels 0.43-2.1.
issues.why_it_matters: A false detection or band mismatch affects radio-emitter and spectral comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Use nondetection and primary configured band 0.856-1.712 GHz; preserve Ridder band as discrepancy until intent is known.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 has 1-10 flux 1.7+/-0.4e-13 and 0.1-10 2.1+/-0.6e-13. Its section 3.2 describes 2SXPS hardness/model conversions. Exact 2SXPS 142122 has observed 0.3-10 PowFlux 1.248+/-0.331e-13 and unabsorbed 2.474+/-0.656e-13. 0.1-10 extrapolates below Swift/XRT 0.3 keV; historical HEAO flux was transient/high.
issues.why_it_matters: X-ray/radio comparisons depend on band, absorption, spectrum, state and epoch.
issues.needed_action: Keep native and converted values separate; choose uniform comparison band/model/state treatment. Trace exact Ridder object-level conversion if possible.

issues.competing_evidence: Hewitt+20 Table 4 lists Mdot=6e-9 Msun/yr; section 4.5 says rate was varied and selected by visual SED resemblance, not fit, with WD/donor light omitted.
issues.why_it_matters: Model input could be mistaken for measured Mdot in accretion/evolution comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Retain only as an SED-model-selected rate unless an independent direct Mdot estimate is located.

issues.competing_evidence: Thoroughgood+05 full text checked; Diaz & Hubeny+99 and Mauche+94 original full texts not retrieved. Still+98 publisher metadata/abstract checked; its full article not independently read. Related claims are secondary reports.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor subtype, distance/extinction and spiral claims have weaker provenance than directly checked mass/orbit/radio papers.
issues.needed_action: Obtain and check Diaz & Hubeny+99 and Mauche+94 original tables if needed for public claims; otherwise retain as explicitly secondary.

references.note: MeerKAT study of 11 novalike CVs; local PDF text audited for CM Phe table values Porb=0.2689(7) d, distance 315.1 +/-3.8 pc, radio non-detection <30 microJy at 0.43-2.1 GHz, radio luminosity upper limit 4.6e15 erg/s/Hz, Hoard+01 M2-5 donor citation, identity-confusion note, and disk SED assumptions Mwd=0.75 Msun, M2=0.5 Msun, i=57 deg, Mdot=0.7e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for IM Eri: Table 1 gives distance 191.2 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.1456348(4) d from Armstrong+13_IMEri; Section 2.5 identifies IM Eri as a non-eclipsing novalike with blue-shifted He I 5876 and super/suborbital signals; Table 3 gives first radio detection 99 +/-26 microJy, Lnu=4.3 +/-1.1e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=1.2 +/-1.6; Table 4 uses assumed M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.24 Msun, i=57 deg, Mdot=2.5e-9 Msun/yr for a disk SED model and notes the IM Eri Mdot is particularly uncertain because no UV data and assumed binary parameters. Audited for V347 Pup: Table 1 gives distance 295.8 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.231936060(6) d from Thoroughgood+05_V347Pup; Section 2.9 summarizes eclipsing novalike/SW Sex-like nature, possible historical IP suggestion but no coherent optical pulsations/no strong magnetic evidence, q=0.83 +/-0.05, M1=0.63 +/-0.04 Msun, M2=0.52 +/-0.06 Msun, i=84.0 +/-2.3 deg, and M0.5V donor; Table 3 gives radio non-detection <30 microJy; Section 4.1 notes a weak 28 +/-14 microJy signal was rejected as below 5sigma/offset/not beam-consistent; Table 4 uses Mdot=6e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for IX Vel: Table 1 gives distance 90.6 +/-0.2 pc and Porb=0.193929(2) d from BeuermannThomas+90_IXVel; Section 2.1 describes IX Vel as brightest night-sky CV, gives M1=0.80 +0.16/-0.11 Msun and M2=0.52 +0.10/-0.07 Msun from Beuermann & Thomas, Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr and i=57 +/-2 deg from Linnell+07_IXVel, and P-Cygni UV wind outflows ~3000 km/s; Table 3 gives MeerKAT non-detection <42 microJy and Lnu<0.4e15 erg/s/Hz; Section 4.4 gives SED-preferred Mdot~7e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for RW Sex: Table 1 gives distance 236.5 +/-5.0 pc and Porb=0.24507(20) d from Beuermann+92_RWSex; Section 2.7 summarizes non-eclipsing novalike, q=0.74 +/-0.10, i=28-40 deg, Linnell+10_RWSex Mdot~5e-9 Msun/yr, K5 donor spectrum from VandePutte+03_RWSex, and disk wind ~4550 km/s; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz integrated radio flux 82 +/-23 uJy, Lnu=5.5 +/-1.6e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=-1.5 +/-1.0; Table 4 SED-model parameters use M1=0.84 Msun, M2=0.62 Msun, i=34 deg, and Mdot=8e-9 Msun/yr, while text notes Linnell+10 optimum Mdot=5.75e-9 Msun/yr at old Hipparcos distance and that Gaia lowered the distance. Audited for LS IV -08 3: Table 1 gives distance 211.0 +/-2.8 pc and Porb=0.1952894(10) d from Stark+08_LSIV-08-3; Section 2.6 describes it as an optically bright novalike with no previous radio observations; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz nondetection <33 microJy and Lnu<1.8e15 erg/s/Hz; Table 4 uses assumed/default SED parameters M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.45 Msun, i=57 deg, and Mdot=5e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for V341 Ara: Table 1 gives distance 156.1 +/-2.0 pc and Porb=0.15216(2) d from BondMiszalski+18_V341Ara; Section 2.3 summarizes novalike classification plus Fr 2-11 and bow-shock nebula context; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz nondetection <27 microJy and Lnu<0.8e15 erg/s/Hz; Table 4 uses assumed/default SED parameters M1=0.75 Msun, M2=0.27 Msun, i=30 deg, and Mdot=3.5e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for V3885 Sgr: Table 1 gives distance 132.7 +/-1.4 pc and Porb=0.20716071(22) d from RibeiroDiaz+07_V3885Sgr; Section 2.2 summarizes Hartley+05_V3885Sgr q/mass/inclination constraints and Linnell+09_V3885Sgr Mdot=5 +/-2e-9 Msun/yr; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz detection 256 +/-25 uJy, Lnu=5.4 +/-0.5e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=-0.6 +/-0.7; Table 4 uses SED inputs M1=0.675, M2=0.473, i=60 deg, and Mdot=8e-9 Msun/yr; text summarizes earlier ATCA detections from Koerding+11_V3885Sgr. Audited for V5662 Sgr: Table 1 gives distance 168.6 +/-5.2 pc, Porb=0.062887(37) d from Tappert+04_CTCV, V=15.4-18.0, and M_V=9.3-11.9; Section 2.4 calls it faint/little-studied with shortest period in sample, notes unusually strong H-alpha and possible missed-outburst dwarf nova status; Table 3 gives MeerKAT 0.43-2.1 GHz non-detection <24 uJy and Lnu<0.8e15 erg/s/Hz; Table 4 uses assumed/default SED inputs M1=0.75, M2=0.09, i=57 deg, Mdot=0.005e-9 Msun/yr. Audited for V603 Aql: Table 1 gives distance 313.4 +/-6.7 pc and Porb=0.1382009(4) d from Peters & Thorstensen (2006); Section 2.10 repeats Arenas+00 q=0.24 +/-0.05, M1=1.2 +/-0.2 Msun, M2=0.29 +/-0.04 Msun, i=13 +/-2 deg and Retter & Naylor Mdot=9.2e-9 to 9.47e-8 Msun/yr. Table 3 gives MeerKAT detection 233 +/-36 uJy at 0.43-2.1 GHz, Lnu=27 +/-4e15 erg/s/Hz, alpha=0.2 +/-1.1; Table 4/SED model uses M1=1.2, M2=0.29, i=13, and preferred disk Mdot~3e-9 Msun/yr. IX Vel Table 2/3 checked: MeerKAT on 2018-10-31 00:44:37.1 UTC for 6246 s; 0.43–2.1 GHz integrated limit <42 uJy, RMS 14 uJy/beam, beam 5.9x4.1 arcsec, PA -50.3 deg. Published Lnu <0.4x10^15 erg s-1 Hz-1 uses 90.6 pc. No spectral index for the nondetection.; V341 Ara: Table 2 has MeerKAT start/integration; Table 3 gives 0.43-2.1 GHz <27 uJy integrated non-detection and Lnu<0.8e15 erg s-1 Hz-1 using 156 pc. Table 4 SED inputs (M1=0.75, M2=0.27 Msun, i=30 deg, Mdot=3.5e-9 Msun/yr) are assumptions, not measurements.

Table4 reports no SU UMa flux errors or epoch/state; values are non-simultaneous with 2015 VLA data.; SU UMa Table 4 X-ray reference [5] is Collins & Wheatley (2010), not a source-specific XMM detection.
